name: Undersea cables & GPS
value: Fitburg crew jailed; no new cut found
summary: Finnish court jailed Fitburg's captain over Baltic cable damage on 5 Nov; no new cable cut found to 18 Nov
state: Helsinki District Court on 5 Nov sentenced the Fitburg's Russian captain to three and a half years over the 31 Dec 2025 anchor-dragging that damaged Gulf of Finland telecom cables, and also convicted a second crew member; both deny wrongdoing (Euronews; Yle, 5 Nov). Searches on 18 Nov found no new cable cut and no major new GNSS jamming escalation. The ruling concerns a past incident, so Watch holds rather than rising.
for_you: Cable damage rarely cuts UK internet access because traffic reroutes. Pilots and mariners in the Baltic follow official notices on GPS interference.
rubric_hit: Watch: cable damage incident (court ruled on 5 Nov on Fitburg sabotage of Dec 2025); no multiple cuts isolating a region

sources.title: Euronews — Finnish court jails Russian captain over Baltic Sea cable sabotage
Yle — Fitburg captain sentenced over Gulf of Finland cable damage

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
